title: Starlink Mini on a Kayak at Full Throttle: Does It Keep Up? (Part 2)
description:
This is Part 2. In Part 1, a 30 W USB outlet couldn't boot my Starlink Mini. This time I wired it properly to a 12V, 300 Wh LiFePO4 battery and left it running on my kayak all morning: through the launch, a full-throttle run on the Minn Kota, five hours of fishing, and the ride back in.

The watt meter stayed inline the whole time: about 20 W on average, a 47.98 W peak after the full-throttle test, and the dish was still running when I hit the trailer, a bit over 6 hours after I turned it on. I forgot the action-cam SD card and didn't screen-record the speed tests, so the only speed-test screen in this video is the parked Nov 1 run (165 down / 11 up). Bass count: 6. The rock test is still on the to-do list.

title: Can a Homelab Nerd Put Starlink on a Kayak? (Part 1)
description:
I have internet in my house. I have internet in my car. So why not my kayak? 🛰️

Part 1 of my Starlink-on-a-kayak side quest. I'm a homelab guy, so I treat the Starlink Mini like a server install. I unbox it, launch at Boerne City Lake, and put a USB-C watt meter on it to see what it really pulls (73.8 W at peak). Then the Anker power bank runtime test (about 3 hours), and my 12V battery plus USB outlet that should've been the backup plan. Spoiler: a 30 W USB-C port won't boot a Starlink Mini. Doh.

So does it actually work out on the water? Stick around for the first speed test at the launch.

Part 2: the 12V battery on the water, and whether I can shake it offline.

title: The Big One Got Away!
description:
One landed. One got away.

A calm October morning working a brushy shoreline on Canyon Lake, TX from the kayak. A small largemouth comes aboard first and goes right back in. About 18 minutes later, a much bigger bass hits, jumps right beside the kayak, and throws the hook. There's a slow-mo replay too, so you can feel my pain 😅

I kept score this time. Final tally: Big Bass 1, Dan 0.

title: Sunrise Launch, Sunfish & a Creek Run | First Cold Front Kayak Trip
description:
My first fall cold front trip, about 50°F at launch. That counts as cold in Texas 🥶

It starts with the kayak and the trailer, then a sunrise launch on Boerne City Lake in Boerne, TX. The water was 67, down from 85 not that long ago. I get the first small fish of the day, then a sunfish with a big attitude by the reeds. After that I head up the creek for a morning cigar (a Texas Sweets), cast into some moving water, and make a brisk ride back.

Two fish. One cold front.

title: The Cigar Side Quest | Cigars on the Kayak, Zero Fish on Camera
description:
Main quest is fishing, side quest is cigars.

Two mornings on the kayak, a couple of cigars, and zero fish on camera. The cigars took this round 😅

On the first morning I light a breakfast cigar on a moving kayak, scout some points and a cove, and admit I can't pick out tasting notes. I just know what I like. Water temps are finally dropping, and the Connecticut wrapper was nice and gentle.

The second morning is my first cold front trip of the season, with a Texas Sweets on the water and a Montecristo White Label saved for the ride back. It's windy, so don't judge the torch. I also share how this side quest started about 25 years ago, and why the real Cubans I tried in Taiwan never won me over.

Rigs: Texas rig, Ned rig with a paddle tail
